clue.text: A young creature first seen in this island _

indicators.note: first tells us the young creature comes before the A in the answer

parts.note: a cub is the young of a fox, bear or lion

explanation.surface: A fox cub is the first thing a visitor spots on arrival at some island.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 3 across with its trailing dots. 'first' puts CUB ahead of A, though the clue gives A first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the Caribbean's largest island nation, which the clue points at as this one.

clue.text: Beat Australian friend across lake

indicators.note: across says the friend stretches over the lake, so the lake goes inside

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate or friend
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone gets hit by an Aussie mate on the far side of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is slang for hitting them hard, a synonym of beat.

clue.text: Continue playing cricket for the staff

parts.note: to bat is to play as the batsman in cricket
on, as in carry on, means continue

explanation.surface: A cricketer stays in to keep batting on behalf of the team's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'bat on' is to continue batting in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or rod, the staff carried by a conductor or relay runner.

clue.text: - and this bird lives in the same place, initially

indicators.note: initially says the same-place abbreviation comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: ib. (short for ibidem) is the scholarly abbreviation meaning in the same place
lives means is, exists

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a bird shares the island with the young creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The scholarly footnote abbreviation for ibidem can be cut to just its first two letters; 'initially' sets it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a down-curved bill, so it is the bird named here.

clue.text: Gentle way to approach end of decade, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and the spelling changes

parts.words: way to approach end of decade
parts.note: the ninth year is the last before a decade ends, so to approach that end is to be nine

explanation.surface: Advice on the kindest way to near the close of a ten-year span.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be nine' is how one reaches the last year of a decade; spoken, it gives the spelling BENIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign describes a kindly, mild temperament, a synonym of gentle.

clue.text: Foolish to accept damaged net without saying anything

indicators.note: to accept means the foolish word takes the other letters within it

parts.note: silly means foolish

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of net are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly agrees to take a torn net, never voicing a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the anagram and 'to accept' the container; 'without saying anything' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Silently means making no sound, which is the same as uttering no word.

clue.text: About time grazing animal is put off

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the animal goes round the time letter

parts.note: a deer is an animal that grazes

explanation.surface: A grazing beast gets driven away after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage, so someone put off has been dissuaded.

clue.text: Sceptic studying modern poet, but confused inwardly

indicators.note: inwardly means the jumbled letters go inside the studying word

parts.note: doing a subject means studying it, as in doing French at university

indicators.note: confused says the letters of but are mixed up

parts.note: Dylan Thomas was a twentieth-century Welsh poet

explanation.surface: A reader studying a contemporary poet ends up muddled within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' is the anagram signal and 'inwardly' the container; 'studying' as doing is the British sense of taking a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection without proof gave his name to any habitual disbeliever.

clue.text: Dreary activity, initially, to study economics

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word to

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
John Stuart Mill wrote Principles of Political Economy, so his name stands for economics

explanation.surface: Reading economics feels like a dull grind from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: J. S. Mill was the Victorian philosopher and economist.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any monotonous routine that goes nowhere.

clue.text: Substitute book

definitions.meaning: a stand-in player kept back for a team
to book is to secure a place or table in advance

explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is a spare player, and to reserve a seat is to book it.

clue.text: Vacillate like certain fans?

definitions.meaning: a fan heater can push out warm air or cool air

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wavers keeps switching enthusiasm on and off, like a heater with two settings.

clue.text: Bunting taken from door to landing

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the words door to landing

explanation.surface: Someone takes down festive flags along the way from the front door to the upstairs landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' looks like flags; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family, once a gourmet delicacy.

clue.text: Literary man's honour — not Hardy's, however?

definitions.text: Literary man's honour — not Hardy's, however?

parts.words: Literary man's honour — not Hardy's, however?
parts.note: a poet's crown of bay leaves, read as the possessive of the thin partner of Oliver Hardy in the comedy double act rather than of Hardy himself

explanation.surface: A writer receives an accolade that the novelist Thomas Hardy never won.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy misleads as Thomas Hardy, the novelist; the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy gives the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurels are the wreath of bay awarded to poets, hence any honour or distinction.

clue.text: Humorist in desert without a vehicle to jump on

indicators.note: in places the joker inside the shortened word for desert
without says the word for desert loses its letter a

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
the letter a as written
a wag is a joker or humorist

explanation.surface: A comic stranded in the desert lacks any transport to hop aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' signals the dropped letter and 'in' the container; one jumps on a bandwagon, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump on the bandwagon is the idiom for joining a popular cause; the original was a wagon carrying a band.

clue.text: Royal house party held in rejection of dreary routine

indicators.note: held in puts the party inside the turned-around routine
rejection here means throwing back, so the routine word is turned around

parts.note: a rut is a dull, unvarying routine
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A palace throws a party as a break from tedious daily life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' reverses RUT into TUR, and DO is 'held in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the dynasty that ruled England from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Beak given the staff that's required to press charges

parts.note: a ram is the beak or projecting prow of a warship
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A magistrate and his officers are needed to bring a prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which suits 'press charges'; here it is a ship's ram. The charges are gunpowder loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is the rod used to push the powder and ball down the barrel of a muzzle-loading gun.

clue.text: Infuriating, like Gray's crowd concealing directions

indicators.note: concealing means the crowd's word hides the directions within it

parts.note: Thomas Gray's Elegy speaks of the madding crowd, frenzied and wild
E and N are the compass directions east and north

explanation.surface: Gray's crowd hiding its bearings is enough to drive anyone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard has the line 'Far from the madding crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something maddening drives one wild with annoyance, so it is infuriating.

clue.text: Source of gold king found on leaving capital with president

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: leaving says the word on departs from the name of the capital

parts.note: London is the capital of the United Kingdom
the word on as written
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A monarch turns up with the president after quitting the capital, chasing gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes ON from LONDON to leave LOND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Klondike in Canada's Yukon was the scene of the great 1890s gold rush.

clue.text: Disposed to use bar, he inflicts malicious damage

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to wield a crowbar turns out to be a vandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed' reads as inclined; it means arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur is one who deliberately wrecks equipment or plans.

clue.text: Vessel a serving-girl carried back into pub

indicators.note: into puts the reversed letters inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: carried back means the words a and serving-girl are turned round

parts.note: the letter a as written
a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A barmaid ferries a container back into the tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried back' reverses A MAID into DIAMA, put 'into' INN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant sailing ship trading with India.

clue.text: Expand home, adding fifth apartment

parts.note: in means at home
a flat is an apartment
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A family grows its living space by adding a fifth flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate is to blow up or swell, making something larger.

clue.text: Unemotional type originally employed in firm

indicators.note: employed in puts the selected letter inside the firm word

parts.note: solid means firm

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of type

explanation.surface: A dispassionate kind of person first took a job with a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company; it means solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes someone impassive who shows little feeling.

clue.text: Hopelessness Christian had to combat

definitions.meaning: the giant who imprisons the hero of Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress in Doubting Castle

explanation.walkthrough: Christian is the pilgrim in Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress, not any believer.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter loss of hope, and Giant Despair is Christian's foe in Bunyan's allegory.

clue.text: Work of art university displayed in ceremonious style

indicators.note: displayed in says the university letter is shown within the ceremony word

parts.note: state means grand ceremony, as in lying in state

explanation.surface: A sculpture is unveiled at a university with great pomp.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a piece of art.

clue.text: An Irish composer's range of activities

definitions.meaning: John ..., the Dublin-born composer who invented the nocturne
an area of work or interest, as in one's chosen line

explanation.definitionFit: John Field was an Irish composer, and a field is one's sphere of work.

clue.text: Extrovert son's expenditure

parts.note: an extrovert person is outgoing

explanation.surface: A sociable lad spends heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': son has expenditure.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are the sums of money that are spent, so they form expenditure.

clue.text: An old chestnut may produce this sort of laugh

definitions.text: An old chestnut may produce this sort of laugh

parts.words: An old chestnut may produce this sort of laugh
parts.note: a stale joke seems to invite a groan, but the chestnut is an aged reddish-brown horse, whose cry sounds like a horse-laugh

explanation.walkthrough: A chestnut is both a tired joke and a reddish-brown horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry of a horse, and a coarse guffaw is called a horse-laugh.

clue.text: Fatty is a dope, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A rude remark about an overweight person being stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means consisting of or relating to fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Empress, way back, with name enshrined in song

indicators.note: back means the way abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: enshrined in places the name letter inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: An empress of long ago has her name preserved in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ST to TS; 'way back' looks like 'long ago'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar, or a female ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Played a risky stroke, showing keenness

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to edge the ball is to nick it off the side of the bat

explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who edged nicked the ball, and an edged blade is sharp.

clue.text: Reduce sail, seeing hazard at sea

definitions.meaning: to roll up part of a sail to cut its area
a ridge of rock or coral just below the water

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors reef sails in strong wind, and a reef is a submerged ridge that wrecks ships.

clue.text: Fish in burn

definitions.meaning: a trout-like freshwater fish of cold lakes

explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like the Scottish word for a stream, a fishy place; it means scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a salmon-family fish, and to char wood is to burn it.
